Theorem
[Local injectivity-radius bound] Source: cheeger-gromov-taylor:page-0032, cheeger-gromov-taylor:page-0033 1. Theorem 4.3\group section-4

Let $B_r(p)$ be as above. If $\gamma $ is a geodesic loop on $p$ of length $2l$, and $r_0+2s \le r$, $r_0 \le r/4$, then \begin{equation} \tag {4.21} l \ge \frac{r_0}{2}\, \frac{1}{1+V^0_{r_0+s}(p)/V_s(p)}. \end{equation} If in addition $H < K_M \le K$, then \begin{equation} \tag {4.22} l \ge \frac{r_0}{2}\, \frac{1}{1+V^H_{r_0+s}(p)/V_s(p)}. \end{equation}

Proof

Source: cheeger-gromov-taylor:page-0033 \sketch For a loop with $L(\gamma )=2l<r_0$, set $N=\lfloor r_0/(2l)\rfloor $. Lemmas 22, 22, and 22 give at least $N$ inverse images of each point of $B_s(p)$ in $B_{r_0+s}(0)$. Since $\exp _p$ is nonsingular and orientation preserving, $N V_s(p)\leq V^0_{r_0+s}(p)$; rearranging and using volume comparison yields (4.21) and (4.22).

□

For $r$ below the conjugate radius, the Gauss lemma identifies $B_r(0)\subset T_pM$ with radial geodesics from $p$. Write $c_1\sim _Ac_2$ when the curves are homotopic relative endpoints through curves of length at most $A$; the radial lift of a curve of length $<r$ is unique. Since $\exp _p$ is nonsingular on $B_r(0)$, distinct radial geodesics represent distinct such classes. Write $[c]$ for the radial representative and $[p]$ for the constant loop.

Let $\theta _1,\theta _2$ be closed curves on $p$, and let $c$ be an arc from $p$ with $L[\theta _i]\le 2l$, $L[c]=s$ and $2(l+s)<r$. Let $\theta _i \cup c$ denote the arc from $p$ which is equal to $\theta _i$ followed by $c$.
